name: SHT45 precision temperature & humidity sensor
description: Sensirion SHT45 (SHT4x family, best accuracy grade) digital temperature (-40 to 125 °C, ±0.1 °C typical) and relative humidity (0–100 %, ±1.0 % typical) sensor with an I2C interface at the fixed address 0x44. The chip runs on 1.08–3.6 V; the breakout adds a 3.3 V regulator, level shifting and 10 kΩ pull-ups so it runs from 3.3–5 V. Sold as: Adafruit Sensirion SHT45 Precision Temperature & Humidity Sensor - STEMMA QT / Qwiic (#5665; 5-pin header VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCL, SDA, plus two STEMMA QT sockets), same pinout as the Adafruit SHT40/SHT41 boards.
eli5: Tells your board how warm the air is and how damp it is, extremely accurately.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 3.3–5 V (on-board 3.3 V regulator; use the same voltage as your board's logic)

pins.name: 3Vo
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board regulator (up to 100 mA); not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up and level shifter on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up and level shifter on the board)

supplierQuery: Adafruit SHT45 precision temperature humidity sensor STEMMA QT 5665
buildNotes: Single-shot high-precision command is one byte, 0xFD; wait at least 8.3 ms (10 ms is safe) before reading 6 bytes: temperature MSB, LSB, CRC, humidity MSB, LSB, CRC.
Check each CRC (poly 0x31, init 0xFF). A mismatch almost always means a loose SDA/SCL wire.
Humidity is RH = -6 + 125 × raw / 65535 and can come out slightly below 0 or above 100 %: crop it to 0–100 % as the datasheet advises.
The address is fixed at 0x44 on this board, so only one SHT45 per I2C bus.
Leave 3Vo unconnected; it is the regulator's output, not a supply input.
Keep the sensor away from the board's regulator and the ESP32, which warm the air around them.

driver.code:
# SHT45 precision temperature & humidity sensor (Sensirion SHT4x), MicroPython driver.
# Single-shot, high-precision measurement (command 0xFD, max 8.3 ms), CRC-8 checked as in the
# datasheet (poly 0x31, init 0xFF). Conversion: T = -45 + 175*S/65535 degC, RH = -6 + 125*S/65535 %,
# RH cropped to 0..100 % as the datasheet advises. Works for SHT40/SHT41/SHT45 alike.
import time


def _crc8(data):
    crc = 0xFF
    for b in data:
        crc ^= b
        for _ in range(8):
            crc = ((crc << 1) ^ 0x31) & 0xFF if crc & 0x80 else (crc << 1) & 0xFF
    return crc


class SHT45:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x44):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        time.sleep_ms(1)  # power-up time, max 1 ms

    def _read6(self):
        d = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 6)
        if _crc8(d[0:2]) != d[2] or _crc8(d[3:5]) != d[5]:
            raise OSError('SHT45 CRC mismatch: check the wiring')
        return d

    def reset(self):
        """Soft reset (0x94); the sensor is idle again after at most 1 ms."""
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\x94')
        time.sleep_ms(1)

    def serial_number(self):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\x89')
        time.sleep_ms(1)
        d = self._read6()
        return (d[0] << 24) | (d[1] << 16) | (d[3] << 8) | d[4]

    def read(self):
        """Measure once and return (temperature in degC, relative humidity in %)."""
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\xfd')
        time.sleep_ms(10)  # high precision takes up to 8.3 ms
        d = self._read6()
        t_ticks = (d[0] << 8) | d[1]
        rh_ticks = (d[3] << 8) | d[4]
        t = -45 + 175 * t_ticks / 65535
        rh = -6 + 125 * rh_ticks / 65535
        rh = min(max(rh, 0.0), 100.0)
        return t, rh

    def temperature(self):
        return self.read()[0]

    def humidity(self):
        return self.read()[1]

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from sht45 import SHT45

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = SHT45(i2c)
while True:
    t, h = sensor.read()
    print('T=%.1fC H=%.0f%%' % (t, h))
    time.sleep(1)
